Assessment & Plan (Integrating DDx)

- 26-year-old man with known asthma presents with acute chest tightness, wheeze, cough and mild exertional dyspnea after 1 week without inhalers and recent viral URI. No distress at rest.  
- Working diagnosis: Acute asthma exacerbation precipitated by viral infection and lapse in inhaled therapy.  
- DDx aligned with presentation:  
  • Acute asthma exacerbation – High likelihood (see above).  
  • Viral acute bronchitis with reactive airways – Moderate likelihood (persistent post-viral cough; overlaps with asthma flare).  
- Low-likelihood considerations (from DDx): Community-acquired pneumonia, pulmonary embolism (no findings supporting these currently).  
- Management priorities: Rapid bronchodilation, anti-inflammatory therapy, re-establish regular inhaler use, education on spacer and action plan, safety-net advice, arrange follow-up.  

Management Plan

- Prescriptions sent:  
  • Salbutamol (Ventolin) inhaler – PRN for wheeze.  
  • Beclomethasone (Clenil Modulite) inhaler – maintenance (dose not documented).  
  • Oral corticosteroid course for 5 days (two tablets each morning; specific steroid and dose not documented).  
  • Spacer device with written instructions.  
- Education: Review of correct inhaler/spacer technique; advised to use Clenil regularly once recovered and Ventolin only PRN; seek urgent care if Ventolin needed more often than q3 h or if symptoms worsen.  
- Sick note/allow rest from work or study.  
- Follow-up: Not specifically scheduled; advised to seek further medical review if deterioration occurs.

Summary of Differential Diagnoses (from DDx):

1. Acute asthma exacerbation – High: Classic asthma symptoms, history of asthma, recent trigger (viral URI) and medication lapse.  
2. Viral acute bronchitis with reactive airways – Moderate: Ongoing post-viral cough/wheeze; could coexist with asthma flare.
